main_body: Timber-framed house: a large tiled hip roof slope over a plaster half-timbered upper storey and a stone-block ground floor with a door
top_band: At x=48, rows 1-42 are a brown tiled roof slope (L 104 with dark L 43 tile joints) under a 1px near-black outline. Rows 43-45 are a dark eave line. Below that is the cream wall face (L 189).
evidence: The big roof slope is a foreshortened horizontal-ish surface seen from above, like the hip roofs on the references. A dark eave band (rows 43-45) and a lighter brown wall-plate row separate it from the front wall. The wall is clearly lighter than the roof, a step of about 85 L. The windows and the door have dark inner edges and sills, so they read as inset. The roof is about 42 rows and the wall about 62 rows, so both a top and a front face are clearly drawn.

style.evidence: The whole piece uses only 4 distinct colours, against 185 and 66 for the references. Median colours per tile is 3, against 18 and 11. Flat-fill coverage is 17%, against 0%. The outline pixels are 100% near-neutral, against 7-9% for the references, which is the sticker-outline look. The roof is a two-tone checker of one brown and one dark brown, with no highlight, mid or deep ramp and no per-tile shading. The wall and stone areas are flat cream with dark joints and only 2-3 lightness steps. It is much shallower than the Beodeul references.
